info.desc: Robbie Robertson is the self-titled solo debut by Robbie Robertson, released in 1987. The album won the Juno Award for "Album of the Year", and producers Daniel Lanois and Robertson won the "Producer of the Year" Juno award, both in 1989 as there were no Juno Awards held in 1988. The album is notable for the contributions from the members of U2 and Peter Gabriel, both of who were also working with producer Daniel Lanois at the time. U2 were recording The Joshua Tree and Gabriel was recording So. U2's contribution is heard in the song "Sweet Fire of Love" .

podcast.body: This self-titled album from 1987 marked Robertson's most famous solo work and produced a significant alt-rock radio hit during that period. "Robbie's most famous solo work is a self-titled album from 1987."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
